ideas.hypothesis: H4.1 (new Lvl3 H4.1.2: at 10 ep with no cutout, removing label smoothing entirely raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp)
ideas.description: Exploit. Start from the current best recipe (E004: 128/384/576, 10 epochs, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, translate 4, max-autotune + CUDA-graph train step). Change only the label smoothing, from 0.1 to 0.0. Everything else stays fixed, including the epoch count and the schedule.
ideas.expected: Accuracy moves -0.3 to +0.5 pp (central guess +0.2 pp, to ~0.757). Time is unchanged (~8.94 s +/- 0.1). A gain of >= 0.3 pp supports H4.1.2 and adds margin to spend on cutting epochs. A drop means LS 0.1 was already near optimal for 100 classes.

ideas.hypothesis: H4.1 (new Lvl3 H4.1.3: at 10 ep, cutting translate from 4 px to 2 px raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp)
ideas.description: Exploit. Start from the E004 recipe. Change only the GPU random-translate amplitude, from 4 px to 2 px (reflect/zero padding stays the same as now). Label smoothing stays at 0.1, cutout stays off, flip stays alternating, and the epochs stay at 10.
ideas.expected: Accuracy moves -0.4 to +0.5 pp (central guess +0.15 pp). Time is unchanged or slightly lower (<= 0.05 s less, from smaller padding). A gain of >= 0.3 pp supports H4.1.3. A drop of >= 0.3 pp means translate is the one regularizer the under-fitting net still needs.

ideas.hypothesis: H1.1.2 (new Lvl3 H1.1.3: on the regularization-tuned recipe, the slope stays ~0.8-0.9 pp/epoch and time ~0.9 s/epoch, so the 0.753 crossing sits near 9.7-9.8 epochs)
ideas.description: Exploit / map the edge. Start from the E004 recipe. Change only the epoch count, from 10 to 9.5, and rescale the warmup/decay schedule so it still anneals fully (per C0006). This gives the second point of the accuracy-vs-epoch curve for the tuned recipe, which tells us how much margin any later accuracy gain has to buy back.
ideas.expected: Accuracy ~0.750-0.753 (about -0.4 pp), time ~8.5 s (about -0.45 s). It is probably just infeasible. Feasible would be a direct ~5% win. The measured slope then sets how many epochs the gains from I010/I011 can buy back.

ideas.hypothesis: H4 (new Lvl2 H4.4: in the compute-bound, under-fitting regime, smaller batches give more optimizer steps per epoch at nearly the same s/epoch; new Lvl3 H4.4.1)
ideas.description: Exploit. Start from the E004 recipe. Change only the batch size, from 1024 to 768. Keep airbench's per-example lr/wd scaling so the effective hyperparameters stay consistent, rebuild the CUDA-graph capture at the new fixed shape in build, and keep 10 epochs with the schedule tied to the new step count.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.2 to +0.6 pp from ~33% more steps. Time +2-6% (~+0.2-0.5 s) from lower GPU utilization per step. The idea pays off only if the accuracy gain is worth more than ~0.5 epoch (>= 0.45 pp) per 0.45 s spent. Otherwise, a refutation means the batch is not limiting.

ideas.description: Explore. Rewrite of I008 onto the current best recipe. Start from E004 (no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune + CUDA graph). Change only the widths, from 128/384/576 to 128/256/384 (same 3 convs per block), and set the epochs to 12 (schedule rescaled) to make up for the lower capacity. Estimated conv FLOPs per epoch are ~0.62x of the wide net.
ideas.expected: Time ~6.5-7.5 s (about 15-25% below 8.94 s). Accuracy ~0.740-0.755. If it reaches >= 0.753, H1.2.1 is supported and the narrow-and-longer branch becomes the main line. If accuracy is < 0.745, then width buys more than epochs on CIFAR-100 (consistent with C0014), so H1.2 loses confidence.

ideas.description: Explore. Rewrite of I009 onto the current best recipe. Start from E004 (10 epochs, no cutout). Change only the resolution schedule: for the first 50% of steps, downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 (F.interpolate, bilinear, antialias=False) after flip and translate. The remaining steps run at 32 px. Keep the LR schedule tied to step count. Compile and capture CUDA graphs for both input shapes on synthetic data in build so no recompile lands in timed train. Eval stays at 32 px.
ideas.expected: Time falls 10-18% (~0.9-1.5 s, to ~7.5-8.0 s). Accuracy drops 0.2-0.8 pp. A drop of <= 0.3 pp supports H3.2.1 and gives a recipe that can afford +1 epoch while still being faster. A drop of > 0.6 pp, or recompile stalls inside the timed train, refutes it.

ideas.hypothesis: H4 (new Lvl2 H4.5: airbench's CIFAR-10 peak LR is too low for the 100-class short run; new Lvl3 H4.5.1: +30% peak LR raises accuracy >= 0.3 pp at 10 ep)
ideas.description: Explore. Start from the E004 recipe. Change only the peak learning rate of the SGD schedule, multiplying it by 1.3. Warmup fraction, decay shape, wd and momentum stay unchanged. Lookahead is unchanged. This is the cheap peak-LR check suggested by C0013.
ideas.expected: Accuracy moves -0.4 to +0.4 pp (central guess ~+0.1). Time is unchanged. A gain of >= 0.3 pp opens a short LR line search. A result within noise refutes H4.5, so the schedule stays frozen as C0004/C0005 recommend.

drop.reason: Rewritten as a new idea (narrow 128/256/384 at 12 epochs). The old version was built on the superseded cutout/LS-0.2 recipe at 10 epochs, which would underestimate the narrow net. It also compared against an 8.5-epoch wide run that was never feasible.

Rewritten as a new idea on the current best recipe (E004, 10 epochs, no cutout, max-autotune + CUDA graphs with both shapes captured). The old version started from the infeasible 8.5-epoch I001 recipe with cutout, so the comparison would no longer reflect the main line.

structured_output.summary:
State of the search: the best feasible run is E004, at 0.7550 accuracy and 8.94 s. Its margin over the 0.753 cutoff is only 0.2 pp.

Two records disagree with the timing:
- **E004 ran 10 epochs, not 8.5.** The I005/I006 descriptions say "8.5-epoch", but the E004 notebook compares against E003 "at equal epochs", and E003 was 10 epochs. The time also matches 10 epochs with max-autotune. Read E004 and E005 as 10-epoch runs.
- **D002's "+2.45 pp at 8.5 epochs" is wrong** for the same reason. The real gain from regularization is about +1.26 pp at 10 epochs.

Measured trade-offs so far:
- More epochs: about 0.87 pp per epoch, at about 0.9 s per epoch.
- Faster compile: max-autotune with CUDA graphs saves only 2.5%, so the training loop is limited by compute.
- Alternating flip: worth about 0.4 pp.

**Plan.** The main bet (priority 5–4) is to raise accuracy at a fixed cost, then spend that margin on fewer epochs:
- I010: drop label smoothing from 0.1 to 0.
- I011: cut translate from 4 px to 2 px.
- I012 (priority 3): run 9.5 epochs with the schedule rescaled. This adds a second point to the accuracy-vs-epochs curve for the tuned recipe.

A batch-size test (768) checks whether more optimizer steps help in this regime.

**Explore (about 1/3 of the queue).** Two queued ideas are rewritten onto the E004 recipe, replacing I008 and I009:
- Narrower net (128/256/384) trained for 12 epochs. Conv FLOPs are about 0.62× the current net, so time is about 15–25% lower if accuracy holds.
- Train at 24 px for the first half, then 32 px. Both input shapes are compiled in build.

A cheap +30% peak-learning-rate check rounds out the queue. That makes 7 queued ideas, plus I007 (whitening on a 5,000-image subset), which is still running.

**Not added.** Proxy-based data filtering (H3.1) stays out of the queue because the C0015/C0018 cards weigh against it.

**Missing inputs.**
- No uncertainty-committee forecasts came with the inputs, so none of the ideas were shaped by members' disagreements.
- The noise floor from repeating an identical run was never measured. With a 0.2 pp margin, any verdict of 0.3 pp or less should be treated as provisional.
